result_text:
I found four candidates in `96305ff..2be1432`, all minor, so I rated every one a nit. The new schedule, opening-hours and weather code otherwise matches design section 4.1. I checked the weekday order (Sunday is 0 in both `getUTCDay` and `WEEKDAYS`), the overlap of opening periods across weeks, and how drive segments line up with the leg. As asked, I did not run any verification pass over these.

It takes the raw timeline minutes, but scheduleTimeAt() blanks any time at or past 2880, which is two days after the day's midnight. The opening-hours approval and FeasibilityChecker would then work from times the schedule says aren't known. Fix: return null when startMinute or endMinute is 2*MINUTES_IN_DAY or more, the same limit scheduleTimeAt uses.",

The settings schema allows any non-negative number for driveBufferPercent. Fix: round off the float error before the ceil, for example Math.ceil(Number(((minutes * (100 + percent)) / 100).toFixed(6))), or limit the setting to whole numbers.",

findings.summary: openTimeInMinutesOf() can return a number of open minutes for a visit whose times scheduleOf() shows as empty. It takes the raw timeline minutes, but scheduleTimeAt() blanks any time at or past 2880, which is two days after the day's midnight. The opening-hours approval and FeasibilityChecker would then work from times the schedule says aren't known. Fix: return null when startMinute or endMinute is 2*MINUTES_IN_DAY or more, the same limit scheduleTimeAt uses.
findings.failure_scenario: A day runs late enough that a selected stop arrives at minute 2900, which is after midnight of the second calendar day. scheduleOf() shows that stop's startTime and endTime as null, but openTimeInMinutesOf() still returns a count of open minutes for that visit.

findings.summary: With a fractional drive-buffer percent, a buffered drive time can come out one minute too long. Math.ceil((minutes * (100 + percent)) / 100) runs on binary floats, so an exact whole-minute result can pick up a tiny error and round up. The settings schema allows any non-negative number for driveBufferPercent. Fix: round off the float error before the ceil, for example Math.ceil(Number(((minutes * (100 + percent)) / 100).toFixed(6))), or limit the setting to whole numbers.
findings.failure_scenario: driveBufferPercent = 0.1 and a segment is 1000 minutes. The exact answer is 1001, but 1000 * 100.1 / 100 evaluates to slightly more than 1001, so the drive shows as 1002 minutes and every later time moves a minute.

findings.summary: isWeatherOutOfDate() does not refuse a stay that isn't in the itinerary when that stay has no weather text. The class comment says each function refuses such an object. The null-text branch returns early, before anything calls orderOf(). Fix: call this.orderOf(itinerary, stay) first, as endStayOf() and startTimeOf() do.
findings.failure_scenario: Pass a stay from a different itinerary, or a removed stay, that has weatherText === null. The call returns true or false instead of throwing RuleError, so a caller's mistake goes unnoticed.

findings.summary: A stop with no selected place but a set time can show a known time even when it comes after a drive whose time isn't known. The design says nothing after the first such drive has a known time. In #addUnselected, `at` is worked out from #heldUntil, which still holds the end of the last known item. The stop is then listed after the next selected stop's drive, which may be unknown. Fix: when that drive is unknown, blank the times of the waiting stops before adding them in #addSelected and #addLastDrive, or check the intended behavior against design 4.1.
findings.failure_scenario: Partway through a write, before the leg is re-routed: selected stop A ends at 12:00, unselected stop B is set for 13:00, then selected stop C. driveMinutes is null because the leg wasn't routed for the new selection. The schedule reads: drive (null), B at 13:00, C (null). So B shows a time after an unknown drive.
